subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should mobile support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers, or should the first native proxy-auth surface be limited to typed credential schemes such as Basic, Bearer, or fixed service-token fields?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but the permanent contract controls pre-Gateway credentials, secure storage, redaction, forbidden headers, non-gateway isolation, TLS expectations, and platform parity.

options.title: Land reviewed per-gateway headers
options.body: Review the iOS and Android PRs for secure storage, sanitizer behavior, endpoint scoping, non-gateway isolation, and real authenticated-proxy proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth
options.body: Ask the platform PRs to reduce the user-facing contract if arbitrary headers are too broad for mobile clients.

options.title: Defer mobile proxy credentials
options.body: Keep authenticating-proxy header injection unsupported on mobile for now and document accepted deployment alternatives.

recommendation.title: Land reviewed per-gateway headers
recommendation.body: Review the iOS and Android PRs for secure storage, sanitizer behavior, endpoint scoping, non-gateway isolation, and real authenticated-proxy proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the issue and the two current implementation PRs, so he has the strongest current product/security context for the contract decision.
